newsitem.title: ITALY: BancoNapoli shares fail to open on bourse.
newsitem.headline: BancoNapoli shares fail to open on bourse.

text.p: Shares in struggling southern Italian bank Banco di Napoli failed to open on the Milan bourse on Friday as pre-bourse price quotations exceeded the permitted 10 percent daily fall.
The stock's fall comes on the day of an Italian Treasury deadline for interested parties to make a bid for a 60 percent stake in the bank.
Banco di Napoli savings shares, the only ones traded, were registering a theoretical price of 679 lire per share against Thursday's closing level of 749 lire.

The Treasury took temporary control of Banco di Napoli, Italy's largest southern bank, after it unveiled record losses of 3.12 trillion lire ($2.0 billion) in 1995. It plunged a further 674 billion into the red in the first half of this year.

Italian insurer INA and Banca Nazionale del Lavoro have made a joint offer for the 60 percent stake while state-owned credit institute Mediocredito Centrale announced on Thursday it would make an offer as well.
